    Video series · 5 lessons

    LLM Fundamentals

    A free video tutorial from Matt Pocock teaching you the fundamentals of LLM's so you can use them better.

    Start lesson 1
    Matt Pocock

    Watch the intro

    AI is powerful—but weird.

    The tools we have today can already transform the way you work…but they can also get in your way if you don’t understand the fundamentals.

    The tech is both early and developing incredibly fast, which means even the most seasoned developers can get lost in the quirks and constraints.

    If you don't know what those constraints are, you don't know how to work around them, and you're not going to be able to get the most out of the technology that we have.

    These concepts will give you a serious advantage. You’ll pick up the vocabulary people are using, but more importantly, you’ll start thinking about AI in a clearer way.

    Because once you understand the quirks and constraints, you can actually use AI for what it is: a strange but powerful tool that works best when you know its limits.

    What you'll learn

    1. 01What a system prompt really does
    2. 02Why LLMs “think” in numbers, not text
    3. 03Why overstuffing your context window backfires
    4. 04Why giving an LLM too many tools slows it down
    5. 05What an agent is—and when you don’t need one

    5 lessons, in order

    1. 01

      Messages, System Prompts and Reasoning Tokens

      Learn how conversations with AI work under the hood. Explore user messages, system prompts, reasoning tokens, and tool calls.
    2. 02

      What Are Tokens?

      Discover how tokens power LLMs, affecting costs and efficiency. Learn about encoding, decoding, and vocabulary size for optimized text processing.
    3. 03

      What Is The Context Window?

      Discover the context window in AI: input/output tokens, limits, and the "lost in the middle" issue. Optimize token use for better model performance.
    4. 04

      What Are Tools?

      Discover how LLM tools enhance AI capabilities by defining, choosing, and executing tasks via system prompts.
    5. 05

      What Is An Agent?

      Discover the power of agents vs workflows in LLM systems. Learn how agents improvise and workflows optimize for predictable, repeatable tasks.
